column3: བྱེ་བྲག་པ is normally Vaiśeṣika, as the English has it; the context (views from reasoning and absorption, the Brahmajāla scheme) does favour the Vibhāṣā, but the word does not settle it.
སློབ་དཔོན་སློབ་མའི་གཡས་སུ་བསྐོར is literally "to the right of the disciple"; reading it as master and disciple circling clockwise together is possible, not compelled.
The Tibetan has the substance-smeared item floated in the half-filled copper vessel; the English makes the copper vessel the smeared thing and the loose "materials" float.
བདག་མེད་པ་ལོག་པ is "selflessness excluded"; the English's "'not without a self' is reversed" inverts the excluded term.
ཟན་ལ་བལྟས་པ་ཙམ་གྱིས་གནས is the idiom "stay on food alone" (meals, no share of gains); "by looking at the food" is a literal misreading.
ṅit is an indicatory marker on roots that take the ātmanepada endings listed; "a marker indicating a class of verbal endings" is loose but not wrong, and the next sentence says it is on the root.
ཟབ་པར་འདུ་ཤེས་ཤིང་རྣམ་པར་རྟོག་པ་མེད་ན negates both verbs; the English keeps the perception ("perceives them as profound"), and its own next paragraph says "no perception of profundity".
In this Pramāṇa passage on variegated (ཁྲ་བོ) appearances, སྔོན is the standard short form for blue; "earlier" makes worse sense. The English is right.
མི་མཐུན་པའི་ཕྱོགས is the dissimilar case (vipakṣa): the reason is not seen in the passionless. "the counter-argument … is not observed" garbles the logic.
སྔ་འགྱུར here is the earlier translation of this lexicon (beside the Indic copy, རྒྱ་དཔེ); the note "the Old Translation period" misleads, and the two sources are merged into one.
The lemma ལས་བཤད་དེ is glossed "the result will be shown". Both "explained from these" and "the activities are explained" fit the gloss; the commentary does not decide between them.
The following verses reject consort union, so ཕྱག་རྒྱ may well be the karmamudrā partner, but "mudrā and posture" as hand gestures is a possible reading of ཕྱག་རྒྱ་སྟང་སྟབས.
དེ་གནས་པས་ལྡོག་པའམ་རབ་ཏུ་འབྱུང་བ་མེད་པ: what has no cessation or arising (since the substance stays) would have to be called those. The English drops the "there is none" that makes the absurdity.
གསེར་གྱི་གླང་པོས་འགྲོ་བ་ལགས ("goes about on a golden elephant") is on the side and missing from the English question.
དེས་ན་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི … is the lemma "therefore" followed by its gloss; the English quotes the gloss as root text.
དབུགས་དབྱུང is ucchvāsa, a chapter or section ("six chapters condensed from the vast Māyā[jāla]"); "six types of relief" is a literalism that makes no sense.
ལས་ཀྱི་མེ་ལོང་…ལ་ལྟ་བས་ངེས་པར་གཞན་གྱིས་མི་ཤེས་པར: it is settled by looking into the mirror of karma, without others knowing. The English turns the looking into an exception for the ordinary gods.
ཕྱིར་ཞེས་བྱ་བ glosses the root text's དེའི་ཕྱིར ("for its sake"); "the term 'furthermore'" is wrong.
ཨུཏྤ་ལ་ཡི་འདབ་མ་སྔོན་པོ་དེ་དྲངས་ནས is "having drawn that blue utpala-petal", the sword; the English moves the simile onto the hair-cutting.
གཙོ་བོ་མ་ཡིན་པ་བསྟན་པ is "shows the non-principal [sense]"; "this shows his primary qualities" is the opposite.
ཡིད་ནི་རྣམ་པར་གྲོལ་བ་ཡིས། །རྣམ་པར་ཐར་པར་དེས་འདོད is "because the mind is freed, he holds [these] to be liberations"; "One is desired to be liberated" garbles the agent and the sense.
In this offering list ཕྱག beside "joined palms" may be prostration, as the reviewer says, but "gesture" (short for ཕྱག་རྒྱ) is also possible.
སྔགས་པ་འདི་ལྟ་བུ་གསུངས has the honorific གསུངས and is followed by a gloss on the mantra collection: the Blessed One spoke it. "The practitioner spoke in this way" gives the wrong speaker.
The lemma དེ་ཉིད་དུ་ན in a Pramāṇa reply is tattvataḥ, "in reality", which is the point of the answer; "in that very context" loses it.

རྣམ་པར་རྟོག་པ་མེད་པར་སྨྲ་བ་ལ་ནི … ཞེ་ན: the objection is put against the proponent of non-conceptual perception (dative). The English makes that proponent the objector. This is the opponent-voice error.

The English drops "apart from its well-known causes" and frames the causality as observed, but its closing "this is not a certainty" keeps the denial (ངེས་པ་ནི་མ་ཡིན). An omission that weakens the point; not cleanly a reversal.

འཁོར་ལོ་རིན་ཆེན་མཚོ་སྐྱེས་དང་། །རལ་གྲི་ཀ་བ་བརྒྱད་ཀྱིས་བརྒྱན: the four family emblems (wheel, jewel, lotus, sword) adorn the eight pillars. The English merges the jewel and lists the pillars as a fourth emblem.
སངས་རྒྱས་སྤྱན here, beside Māmakī, is the goddess Buddhalocanā; the English translates the name as "the Buddha-Eye" and adds "like that of".
སེམས་དང་བ is prasāda, which covers both serene clarity and faith; "clarity of mind" is an accepted rendering, which the rubric says not to report.
The previous side turns from the nirmāṇakāya to the saṃbhogakāya, so དེ here is the saṃbhogakāya; "this reality" is the wrong referent.
